prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core purpose and constitutional change
- The SNP stands for Scottish independence and more powers for the Scottish Parliament. Electing SNP MPs is presented as a vote for independence; a majority of SNP MPs would trigger a referendum.
- Written constitution with inclusive citizenship; proportional representation at all levels; retain the Queen as Head of State subject to referendum.
- Reduce and democratise quangos; enhance civil service opportunities in an independent Scotland.

Fiscal strategy and public investment
- Create a sovereign wealth fund (Scottish Fund for Future Generations) from oil revenues to fund services sustainably.
- Establish a Scottish Trust for Public Investment to finance infrastructure more cheaply than PFI/PPP.
- Tax: no increase in overall burden without mandate; comprehensive tax review for fairness and simplicity; immediate 10p-per-gallon fuel duty cut funded by a new 5p income tax band over £100k; review local government finance, including local income tax.

Education and students
- Abolish tuition fees and rebuild maintenance grants; implement Cubie recommendations.
- Establish an Education Convention; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18; end league tables; major school refurbishment; support Gaelic-medium education; strengthen inclusion, anti-racism and support for special needs; implement McCrone.

Economy, jobs and workers’ rights
- Target full employment through infrastructure, broadband, skills and streamlined development agencies; promote tourism with better marketing and access.
- Devolve and refocus New Deal; raise minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages; Charter of Trade Union Rights; back EU worker protections.

Environment, water and energy
- Aim for global leadership in sustainability; oppose aspects of UK climate levy impacting hydro; produce a National Environment Plan.
- 12% of energy (25% of electricity) from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear; focus on decommissioning expertise; adopt “six Rs” resource approach.
- Review water charges and governance; halt backdoor privatisation.

Health and care
- Create a National Health Care Commission to set strategy and end postcode treatment; HTBS decisions binding and expanded.
- Preventive health: free fruit for primary pupils; nutritional standards for school meals.
- Free dental check-ups; freeze/review prescription charges; invest in equipment, cleanliness and at least 1,500 more nurses; halve inpatient waiting times.
- Free personal care for all elderly people.

Europe, defence and international
- Pro-EU but oppose a super-state; keep vetoes on resources, tax and constitution; euro only by conditions and referendum. Independence would increase Scotland’s EU representation.
- Remove Trident; oppose US missile defence; phase withdrawal from NATO while maintaining conventional cooperation; create a professional Scottish Defence Force.
- Commercially focused external offices; meet UN aid targets, cancel debt, untie aid.

Society, justice and communities
- Anti-poverty strategy; fair and fast asylum processes.
- Housing debt write-off; devolve housing benefit; oppose wholesale stock transfer; core funding for voluntary sector; tackle homelessness.
- Equality guarantees; expand disability rights and benefits; support carers; consider winter fuel for severely disabled; improve benefit take-up and simplify delivery via a single agency.

Crime and drugs
- Fund 1,000 extra police; strengthen parental responsibility (compensation orders); lifelong restriction for high-risk offenders; faster courts; expand drug courts and treatment.

Rural, agriculture, fisheries and land
- Support rural small businesses, ICT, transport, services; cut fuel duty and address higher rural prices; contingency funds for crises.
- Post–FMD agricultural review; ensure EU level playing field; promote diversification and organics; improve Less Favoured Areas terms.
- Compensated tie-ups, technical conservation, CFP reform with zonal councils; return 6,000 sq miles; salmon farming inquiry.
- Strengthen community rights over land; national freshwater fisheries policy.

Pensions and transport
- Restore earnings link for the basic state pension; smooth winter fuel payments; reduce MIG/pension distortions.
- Regional Transport Authorities; single safety authority; partial public stake in Railtrack; reopen key lines, electrify routes; concessionary fares; targeted road upgrades; reduce ferry fares (RET pilots); more direct flights; abolish Skye Bridge tolls.
